description:
FILED s522b (Opus, 2026-10-20) from the stash-view work (#1510 / #3511, Fable ruling 01:1x: a non-CODE stash element READS as its typeglob).  PRE-EXISTING (the base 8038fac6 answers "" for every row; the tree fixes the plain-expression rows but not the interpolated ones).

Reproducer (scratch/s522b/interp-stash.pl in the s522b worktree):
  package Foo; our $x = 1; sub f {2}
  package main;
  print "[$Foo::{x}]\n";          # perl [*Foo::x]   PCL []
  print "[", $Foo::{x}, "]\n";    # perl [*Foo::x]   PCL (s522b) [*Foo::x], base []
  print "[$Foo::{f}]\n";          # perl [*Foo::f]   PCL []
  my $k = "x"; print "[${'Foo::'}{$k}]\n";   # perl [*Foo::x]  PCL (s522b) [*Foo::x], base []

SILENT WRONG: the interpolated stash element `"$Foo::{x}"` reads as an empty string -- the interpolation scanner (Pl/InterpScan.pm, standing rule: interpolation scanning happens there or not at all) does not route `$PKG::{KEY}` to the stash-element lowering the code path uses (the `%Pkg::` stash arm in Pl/ExprToCL.pm); it probably reads the scalar $Foo:: then a hash subscript on an unrelated %Foo:: hash.  Fix direction: the scanner names the stash element as the code path does (ONE lowering, rule 11).  Bar: the four rows == perl; a guard row in Pl/t/stash-hash-01.t, inverse-verified.
subject: An interpolated stash element "$Foo::{x}" reads "" (perl: the glob *Foo::x) -- the interpolation scanner does not reach the stash-element lowering the code path uses
